findings.title: External feed/article HTML is persisted and rendered without sanitization
findings.body: `import` marks externally supplied `contents` as `raw_html`, and `Post#cook` consequently returns it unchanged. The embed view renders `post.cooked` with `raw`, so scripts, event-handler attributes, iframes, and other active markup from an RSS item or remotely retrieved article execute under the Discourse origin. Feed and article content must be sanitized with the same trusted HTML policy used for normal posts before it is stored/rendered; the URL interpolated into the appended `imported_from` anchor must also be attribute-escaped.

findings.title: Host validation does not protect the remote fetch after redirects
findings.body: The only validation compares the initial URL host to `embeddable_host`, but `TopicEmbed.import_remote` follows that URL with `open(url)`. An allowed-host URL which redirects to an internal address (for example through an open redirect on the embedded site) causes the Discourse server to fetch the internal resource; its response can then be imported into a public topic. Validate every redirect target and resolved connection address against an allowlist, and reject private/link-local destinations.

findings.title: Feed polling uses String#scrub despite the application's Ruby 1.9 compatibility
findings.body: `String#scrub` was introduced in Ruby 2.1. This codebase still documents/supports Ruby 1.9-era execution, so enabling feed polling on those deployments raises `NoMethodError` on the first item and prevents all feed imports. Use a compatible encoding-cleanup implementation or explicitly raise the supported Ruby version before relying on `scrub`.

findings.title: The new controller spec contradicts the asynchronous implementation
findings.body: This example expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` to be called during the request, but `EmbedController#best` now calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` instead. The expectation is never satisfied, so the added spec suite fails. Update the test to assert the enqueue arguments (and retain separate job tests for retrieval), otherwise CI cannot pass and the intended asynchronous contract is untested.
